focus_areas: Species differentiation (Brambling vs Chaffinch) via spatial feature detection
Foot/Branch interaction integrity via topology auditing
Bottom edge text artifact analysis via OCR
custom_prompts_for_reflector: Please pay close attention to the distinction between a female Brambling and a female Chaffinch. The key differentiator is often the rump (white in Brambling, greenish in Chaffinch) and the lack of white outer tail feathers in Chaffinch. Use the open_vocabulary_detector to specifically locate the white rump and wing bars. Also, investigate the garbled text at the bottom using the image_text_auditor—is it a sign of a cropped AI generation or a dataset artifact? Verify that the legs are structurally connected to the branch without fusion artifacts using the topology_boundary_auditor.
image_description: A small passerine bird, identified as a Brambling (Fringilla montifringilla) in non-breeding or female plumage, perched on a thin, mossy branch. The bird displays brownish-grey upperparts, a buff-orange breast, and distinct black wings with white wing bars. A prominent strip of illegible, garbled text artifacts is visible along the bottom right edge of the image.

expert_testimonies.reason: Spatial verification of diagnostic features (white rump, white wing bars) is needed to distinguish from Chaffinch. A classifier alone may miss localized pattern errors.
Crucial to distinguish Brambling from the visually similar Common Chaffinch, especially given the non-breeding plumage which can be confusing.
Replaces animal_pose_auditor. Avian anatomy (wings/tarsi) is not supported by standard pose models. Topology auditor verifies limb connectivity and boundary sharpness effectively.
Specialized tool required for the prominent garbled text artifact identified in observations. Perceptual auditor is insufficient for text-specific analysis.
Holistic quality filter to ensure the 'soft' texture is biological fluffiness and not AI smoothing, complementing the specific text audit.
